first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two independent memories (memory_31, memory_86) show durable, low-risk lifts from simplifying/shortening onboarding for self-serve SMB accounts—this directly addresses two of the three current problems without touching pricing or margin quality. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pressure on price-sensitive SMBs, but its own record flags a pooled-cohort confound from a mid-test redefinition, making its acquisition/revenue-lift numbers unreliable for a one-shot experiment; I want that record verified before ever spending the single weekly slot on it, since pricing moves also carry higher risk of attracting lower-quality, less sustainable revenue. I'm also verifying memory_86 itself since it's the most load-bearing evidence for this week's action and directly overlaps with the current onboarding-completion decline, so confirming its original scope (self-serve accounts, magnitude, any caveats) matters before treating it as durable justification. Referral incentives and activation messaging are viable but address only one symptom each and are less matched to this week's combined onboarding+activation dip; enterprise sales-assist is orthogonal to the SMB pressure described. Given solid (if unverified for nuance) prior replication across two cycles, a standard experiment scale is warranted rather than a small guarded test or broad rollout.
